expected_benefit: ORR 35%, mPFS 8.5 mo, mOS 13.1 mo in the 2L RAS G12 PDAC subgroup at 300 mg (n=26; Wolpin NEJM 2026). G12R sits inside the pooled G12 cohort; no allele-resolved subgroup was published.
key_risks: Any-grade treatment-related AE 96%, grade 3+ 30% across the 168-patient PDAC pool
EGFR-like rash 91% any-grade / 8% G3+
GI toxicity: diarrhea 48%, nausea 43%, stomatitis 31%
Longest follow-up near 2 years; no mature long-term safety for the pan-RAS class
preference_alignment: Strong. Recruiting trial matches prefers_trials; oral once-daily; deepest published on-axis efficacy fits the 0.80 efficacy weight and treat-to-remission goal; no toxicity veto to trip.
guideline_status: Not an NCCN-listed regimen for PDAC and unscored by ESMO. Aligns via the NCCN v2.2026 trial-enrollment principle for actionable-alteration recurrent disease.
rationale_summary: All five personas placed daraxonrasib at rank 1, the only unanimous top pick. It is the one indication-matched, peer-reviewed efficacy signal on the KRAS axis: Wolpin's NEJM 2026 cohort put ORR at 35% with mPFS 8.5 and mOS 13.1 in 2L RAS G12 PDAC at 300 mg, roughly double what second-line chemo delivers. The load-bearing caveat, named by the critic and conservative, is that the 35% is pooled across G12 alleles with no G12R-specific breakdown, and the longest follow-up is about two years. Company and FDA disclosures beyond the dossier (RASolute 302 phase-3 mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40 ITT; FDA Expanded Access Program effective May 2026) strengthen the enrollment rationale but are not peer-reviewed or indexed and are not cited as dossier evidence. The conservative endorsed the pick on its fully characterized, manageable AE table. Access may run through RMC-6236-001, RMC-GI-102, or the Expanded Access route since RASolute 302 is active-not-recruiting.
open_questions: No published G12R-resolved subgroup ORR; the read-across rests on the pooled G12X estimand
RASolute 302 OS and the FDA Expanded Access figures are company/FDA disclosures, not in the dossier evidence files
Practical access route (open trial slot vs expanded access) needs site-level confirmation
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high in 2L G12 PDAC: ORR 35%, mOS 13.1 mo (n=26, pmid:42090791), but G12R-specific rate unpublished so allele-level confidence is lower.

counter_productive_moa.description: Pan-RAS blockade can select adaptive RTK/MAPK reactivation, but no board persona dissented on mechanism grounds.

overall: The only peer-reviewed, indication-matched efficacy on the KRAS axis and the board's unanimous lead; G12R sits inside a pooled G12 estimand rather than its own subgroup.

expected_benefit: Unconfirmed PDAC ORR 40% (n=20) and 42% at the RDE (n=12); 14/14 KRAS G12X patients with >=75% ctDNA reduction, 5 clearing to zero (Erasca topline release, April 2026). Unconfirmed at a 14-week cutoff.
key_risks: No dose-limiting toxicities reported through cutoff
Per-term grade 3+ AE rates not disclosed in the press release
First-in-class cyclophilin-A molecular glue; long-tail toxicity and durability unknown
preference_alignment: Strong on the efficacy axis for this permissive preference set (0.80 efficacy weight, high-risk-high-reward, prefers_trials, oral). Tension: the evidence is a press release, not peer-reviewed.
guideline_status: No NCCN category, no ESMO MCBS score. Trial-enrollment-principle option under NCCN v2.2026.
rationale_summary: This is the sharpest disagreement on the board. The advocate and risktaker rank it second on a 40-42% PDAC ORR and striking ctDNA clearance, corroborating the pan-RAS class on the patient's own primary axis; the critic and concensusite keep it at rank 3 on maturity grounds, and the conservative leaves it off entirely because the grade-resolved AE distribution is undisclosed and no management algorithm exists. The efficacy topline is real but unconfirmed at a 14-week cutoff, G12R is folded into the pooled G12X figure rather than reported on its own, and the whole readout is a single April 2026 Erasca release with no abstract or peer review. The advocate flagged it preference-aligned while the conservative dissented, so this lands as considered_with_caveats: a legitimate same-mechanism enrollment call, not a confirmed second option. Confirm an open PDAC slot at a participating site.
open_questions: Confirmed ORR and durability pending peer-reviewed publication
G12R-specific activity not broken out from the pooled G12X signal
Per-term grade 3+ safety and long-tail tolerability undisclosed
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate but unconfirmed: PDAC uORR 40-42% and 14/14 with >=75% ctDNA drop (nct:NCT06895031), from an April 2026 topline release, not peer-reviewed.
toxicity_burden: Not characterized (no DLTs reported; per-term G3+ rates undisclosed)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pan-RAS glue may drive adaptive RAS-pathway reactivation; ctDNA response has never been shown to translate to RECIST benefit in PDAC.

overall: A second pan-RAS shot on the primary axis with a striking but press-release-only ORR; efficacy corroborates the class while the grade-resolved safety table is still missing.

intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after platinum induction (POLO regimen) — gated on germline BRCA1/2 + platinum
expected_benefit: POLO: PFS HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.35-0.82, p=0.004; 7.4 vs 3.8 mo). Interim OS HR 0.91 (NS). Applies only after a germline BRCA1/2 hit and >=16 weeks of first-line platinum without progression.
key_risks: Grade 3+ AEs 40% (vs 23% placebo); anemia, fatigue, nausea
AE-driven discontinuation 5%
MDS/AML risk (~1.5%) on prolonged PARP exposure
preference_alignment: Mixed. Guideline-preferred and mature-safety, but double-gated and cannot start today — cuts against prefers_trials and treat-to-remission. The risktaker and advocate dissented on preference-fit for exactly this reason.
guideline_status: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 guideline-preferred maintenance (category 2A) for germline BRCA1/2 metastatic PDAC after platinum. The lone drug-level guideline listing on the board.
rationale_summary: This is the guideline-versus-deliverability split. The conservative, critic, and concensusite rank olaparib second because it is the one drug NCCN actually names for this patient and POLO is the only RoB2-low RCT in the dossier. The risktaker and advocate dissent on preference-fit: the pathway is double-gated on a germline BRCA1/2 result not on file and on a platinum induction the patient has never had (adjuvant FOLFIRI was irinotecan-only), so it cannot start for months, and even in-window POLO's interim OS was flat (HR 0.91, NS). Two dissents plus the gating make this considered_with_caveats. Germline testing is a test to order today, not a reason to defer; if it returns BRCA1/2 or PALB2 and a platinum induction holds, this outranks every uncategorized pan-KRAS trial. Rucaparib (rank 9) is the somatic/PALB2 fallback.
open_questions: Germline BRCA1/2/PALB2 status unknown — the germline panel is the gating workup
Patient is platinum-naive; POLO requires a platinum induction to precede maintenance
PFS benefit has not converted to an OS signal even in the registrational population
likelihood_of_effect: Contingent: strong PFS in gBRCA disease (HR 0.53, pmid:31157963) but flat interim OS (HR 0.91), and inapplicable unless germline-positive and platinum-induced.

counter_productive_moa.description: PARP maintenance carries no mechanism that blunts the therapeutic goal; the dissent was preference-fit, not mechanism.

overall: The only guideline-listed drug for this patient, but double-gated on an unordered germline result and an absent platinum induction, so it cannot start today.

expected_benefit: Adds a chemo backbone to the daraxonrasib efficacy above. Depth-of-response precedent from RAMP-205 dose level 1 (5/6 confirmed PRs, n=6; ASCO 2024 abstract) suggests combination intensification reaches deeper responses in RAS-mutant PDAC.
key_risks: Pan-RAS rash/GI stacked on chemo cytopenias and neuropathy
No dedicated PDAC combination-safety readout for the daraxonrasib + chemo backbone
Prior FOLFIRI may push the backbone toward gem/nab if residual neuropathy is present
preference_alignment: Strong. Takes treat-to-remission at face value; oxaliplatin-naive after adjuvant FOLFIRI leaves mFOLFIRINOX biologically on the table; high-risk-high-reward explicitly invited.
guideline_status: Not NCCN-listed; trial-enrollment-principle option under NCCN v2.2026.
rationale_summary: The advocate ranked this third and the risktaker's critique nudged it toward parity with the glue, arguing that for an oxaliplatin-naive remission-seeker the combination's depth-of-response ceiling deserves weight. It rides on the same NEJM daraxonrasib anchor plus the RAMP-205 dose-level-1 preview, which is a striking but tiny 6-patient abstract signal. The conservative's standing watch-item applies: stacking pan-RAS toxicity on chemo without a dedicated combination-safety readout draws qualified dissent on toxicity, so this sits below the monotherapy rank rather than at it. The gate is operational — confirm the PDAC subprotocol is open at the referral site, and let residual neuropathy from prior FOLFIRI steer the backbone.
open_questions: PDAC arm openness varies by site and needs sponsor/treating-team confirmation
No characterized combination-safety profile for daraxonrasib + chemo in PDAC
Backbone choice (mFOLFIRINOX vs gem/nab) depends on residual neuropathy after FOLFIRI
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high on depth of response: chemo-plus-RAS(ON) backbone; RAMP-205 dose-1 5/6 PRs (n=6, abstract; doi:10.1200/JCO.2024.42.16_suppl.4140) previews deeper responses, unproven at scale.

counter_productive_moa.description: Overlapping chemo/RAS toxicity may force dose compromises that erode the intended combination intensity; no mechanism dissent raised.

overall: Combination intensification for a remission-seeking, oxaliplatin-naive patient; a deeper-response ceiling at the cost of stacked, uncharacterized combination toxicity.

expected_benefit: The only regimen hitting three drivers at once — ERK downstream of KRAS G12R plus CDK4/6 dependency from CDKN2A loss and CCND3. Published PDAC signal is stable disease, not response (2 SD, Raybould ASCO 2021, n=26).
key_risks: Overlapping myelosuppression: CDK4/6 cytopenias stacked on MAPK-inhibitor GI toxicity
Grade 3 TRAEs: decreased WBC, decreased lymphocytes, anemia, fatigue (rates untabulated in the abstract)
Common all-grade: fatigue 70%, rash 62%, nausea 54%
preference_alignment: Partial. Recruiting, oral, single regimen covering three of the patient's features, G12R not an eligibility barrier. Tension: best published PDAC signal is stable disease, a lower efficacy prior than the pan-RAS arms.
guideline_status: Off-label, off-guideline combination on a single-arm phase 1.
rationale_summary: Three personas ranked this as the multi-feature swing — the only option touching KRAS, CDKN2A, and CCND3 in one regimen, admitting PDAC by histology so G12R is no barrier. The mechanistic case is the strongest multi-feature fit on the board, but the clinical substrate is thin: the published pancreatic signal was stable disease, not objective response, the toxicity table is abstract-only with per-term G3 rates untabulated, and single-agent palbociclib already failed in CDK4/6-amplified baskets (ORR 4%, O'Hara 2025). The synergy models are G12D/G12V-dominant while G12R runs lower baseline ERK flux, an untested variable. Overlapping MAPK/cytopenia toxicity may force dose compromises that erode the synergy. Ranked here as a deliberate dual-feature keeper, not a data-backed response expectation.
open_questions: No PDAC objective-response readout; the combination rides on organoid/xenograft synergy
G12R-specific synergy data absent; the models are mostly G12D/G12V
Overlapping myelosuppression not characterized in a dedicated PDAC combination-safety publication
likelihood_of_effect: Low for objective response: best published PDAC readout is stable disease (2 SD, n=26; doi:10.1200/JCO.2021.39.15_suppl.3103); rationale is mechanistic, not efficacy-backed.

counter_productive_moa.description: G12R's lower ERK flux may blunt the ERK-inhibitor arm; overlapping toxicity can force dose reductions that undo the vertical blockade.

overall: The only regimen covering KRAS, CDKN2A, and CCND3 together; clean mechanistic logic undercut by a stable-disease-only PDAC signal and G12R-specific uncertainty.

expected_benefit: No efficacy data — first patient dosed April 2026. Oral Switch-II-pocket pan-KRAS inhibitor active against ON and OFF states; PDAC named; eligibility on documented KRAS mutation, so G12R qualifies.
key_risks: No clinical safety data exist yet
Early dose-escalation risks sub-therapeutic starting doses
No G12R-specific activity demonstrated
preference_alignment: Partial. Recruiting, oral, PDAC named, G12R covered by the KRAS-mutation gate. Tension: pure class extrapolation with no efficacy or safety readout.
guideline_status: Not guideline-listed; no pan-KRAS ON/OFF agent is listed for any indication yet.
rationale_summary: The risktaker and advocate hold a slot here as mechanistic optionality on the primary axis — a distinct ON/OFF-active pan-KRAS shot if the RAS(ON) agents hit resistance or intolerable rash. The concensusite dissents on guideline-fit, arguing that ranking a 2026-first-dosed pre-data trial above the guideline-listed olaparib inverts the guideline order; here it sits well below olaparib, so that objection is largely addressed by placement. The honest limit is maturity: no efficacy or safety readout exists, so this rides entirely on the pan-RAS class rationale and G12R's biology sitting in the active-state window. Early-phase slots will be scarce. JAB-23E73 (rank 8) is the near-identical fallback.

G12R-specific activity unproven; eligibility rests on the broad KRAS gate
Dose-escalation slots limited this early in the trial

toxicity_burden: Not characterized (pre-data; no AE table exists)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pan-KRAS inhibition risks adaptive pathway reactivation, but no data and no mechanism-grounded dissent were raised.

expected_benefit: No mature efficacy published; dose-finding. Names G12R explicitly in written eligibility — unusual among first-in-human pan-KRAS programs. 2L+ PDAC monotherapy cohort matches the post-FOLFIRI setting.

Grade 2+ sensory neuropathy is an exclusion — a watch-item post-FOLFIRI, though irinotecan is usually neuropathy-sparing
RP2D in the PDAC cohort still being set

The grade 2+ neuropathy exclusion is a watch-item given prior FOLFIRI, though irinotecan-based regimens are usually neuropathy-sparing. Confirm an open PDAC dose-level slot rather than trusting the global enrollment statement.

toxicity_burden: Not characterized (dose-finding; only protocol exclusions published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pan-KRAS inhibition risks adaptive reactivation; no data and no mechanism dissent.

overall: A first-in-human pan-KRAS program that names G12R in its eligibility criteria; a clean axis backup with no efficacy readout yet.

expected_benefit: No numeric efficacy — only a qualitative 'early antitumor activity' disclosure. Preclinical profile names G12R among covered G12X alleles; spares HRAS/NRAS. Broad KRAS-alteration eligibility admits this RAS-inhibitor-naive patient.
key_risks: No clinical safety data released
Basket enrolls any advanced solid tumor — PDAC slot not guaranteed
No numeric efficacy or per-term AE data

intervention_label: rucaparib maintenance — gated on germline/somatic BRCA1/2 or PALB2 + platinum
expected_benefit: Reiss 2021 phase 2 (n=46): mPFS 13.1 mo, mOS 23.5 mo, ORR 41.7% in the measurable-disease subset. Widens the biomarker net beyond POLO to somatic BRCA and PALB2.
key_risks: Anemia 74% any-grade / 22% G3+
Nausea 48%, ALT elevation 47%, fatigue 45%, thrombocytopenia 39%
PARP-class MDS/AML long-tail risk on prolonged exposure
preference_alignment: Mixed. Same permissive preference set as olaparib, but same double-gate — germline/somatic HRD plus platinum induction — so it cannot start today.
guideline_status: Not category 1 in NCCN PDAC; a fallback to olaparib rather than an equivalent.
rationale_summary: The conservative ranks rucaparib as the PARP-class backup that widens the biomarker net to somatic BRCA and PALB2, covering genotypes POLO excludes. The evidence is phase 2 single-arm rather than an RCT, which is why it sits below olaparib, but the toxicity ceiling is the same well-characterized PARP class with the same MDS/AML long-tail. The same gating logic applies: a germline or somatic HRD hit plus a platinum induction must precede this. Ranked here as the second-line PARP option contingent on the germline panel returning a qualifying variant.
open_questions: Germline/somatic BRCA1/2/PALB2 status unknown
Platinum induction has not occurred
Single-arm phase 2 evidence, not RCT-grade
likelihood_of_effect: Contingent: mPFS 13.1 mo, ORR 41.7% in HRD-positive PDAC (n=46, pmid:33970687), but inapplicable unless germline/somatic-positive and platinum-induced.

counter_productive_moa.description: PARP maintenance carries no goal-blunting mechanism; contingency, not mechanism, limits it.

overall: A PARP backup that broadens the biomarker net to somatic BRCA and PALB2; same germline-plus-platinum double-gate as olaparib, on phase 2 evidence.

intervention_label: anvumetostat (AMG 193, MTA-cooperative PRMT5i) — gated on MTAP co-deletion
expected_benefit: MTA-cooperative PRMT5 synthetic lethality tied to MTAP loss, co-deleted with CDKN2A in ~80-90% of homozygous CDKN2A deletions. NCT06360354 carries a daraxonrasib combination arm covering both KRAS G12R and the CDKN2A-loss/MTAP axis. No PDAC efficacy published.
key_risks: No clinical safety row in the dossier; class-level PRMT5 myelosuppression and GI signal uncharacterized in PDAC
In the daraxonrasib-combination arm, stacked pan-RAS rash/GI with no combination-safety readout
Double-gated: unconfirmed MTAP co-deletion plus the trial's own eligibility
preference_alignment: Partial on mechanism and trial preference, but gated on an unrun MTAP reflex test and carrying no characterized tolerability.
guideline_status: No NCCN category for the class in PDAC; biomarker-plus-trial alignment only.
rationale_summary: The concensusite surfaces the MTAP/CDKN2A synthetic-lethal axis: CDKN2A and MTAP are 9p21 neighbors co-deleted in most homozygous CDKN2A deletions, and the MTA-cooperative PRMT5 class is the synthetic-lethal partner for this patient's CDKN2A loss. The daraxonrasib-combination arm would cover both the KRAS G12R and CDKN2A-loss features in one trial. The conservative's qualifier stands: anvumetostat carries no clinical safety row here, the class is early-phase across every indication, and the pick is double-gated on an unconfirmed MTAP co-deletion. Order the MTAP IHC/NGS reflex; if MTAP is retained the rationale collapses.
open_questions: MTAP co-deletion unconfirmed — reflex IHC/NGS needed
No PDAC-specific PRMT5i efficacy or per-term safety published
Combination-arm tolerability with daraxonrasib uncharacterized
likelihood_of_effect: Contingent and unproven: synthetic-lethal rationale (pmid:26912361, 26912360) is preclinical; no PDAC efficacy, and it collapses if MTAP is retained.
toxicity_burden: Not characterized (no clinical safety row; PRMT5-class myelosuppression/GI expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: Rationale collapses entirely if MTAP is retained rather than co-deleted; combination-arm toxicity uncharacterized.

overall: A synthetic-lethal PRMT5 option for the CDKN2A-loss axis, potentially co-targeting KRAS in one trial; entirely gated on an unrun MTAP reflex test.

expected_benefit: AMPLIFY-201 (n=25): 84% mKRAS T-cell response; RFS/OS not reached in high responders vs 3-16 mo in low responders. G12R directly encoded. All data are in MRD-positive resected disease, not overt recurrence.
key_risks: Zero DLTs and no G3+ vaccine-attributed events — the cleanest safety in the dossier
T-cell response, not tumor shrinkage, is the primary readout
Immunogenicity has not been shown to translate to RECIST response in this disease
preference_alignment: Mechanism-clean for the exact allele and an immune route in MSS disease, but the enrollment window (MRD-positive resected) excludes this overt-recurrent patient — an eligibility mismatch, not a preference conflict.
guideline_status: No guideline endorses a KRAS vaccine in recurrent PDAC.
rationale_summary: The vaccine axis is ranked last and mainly to document why it does not go higher. The mechanism-fit for the exact G12R allele is unusually clean and an immune route is one of the few things that could produce durable control in MSS disease where checkpoint monotherapy is dead — which is why the risktaker, conservative, and critic kept it on their lists. But every human datum sits in the MRD-positive adjuvant window, and this patient is overtly recurrent, outside the enrollment window; the registered ELI-002 7P cohort is active-not-recruiting. AMPLIFY-201's survival separation is a below- vs above-median T-cell responder split, a post-hoc immunogenicity subgroup the critic discounts. The concensusite and advocate treat it as an eligibility mismatch and hold it off their active lists. The related mKRASvax + dual-checkpoint route (NCT06411691) fails the ECOG-0 and prior-metastatic-line gate and adds a 17% G3 irAE cost, so it is not surfaced as a separate rec. Reachable only via a recurrent-setting protocol.
open_questions: No evidence a vaccine controls overt bulk recurrent PDAC
Registered cohort enrolls MRD-positive resected disease and is active-not-recruiting
Survival signal rests on a post-hoc T-cell-responder subgroup
likelihood_of_effect: Low in this setting: strong immunogenicity (84% T-cell response, pmid:40790272) but only in MRD-positive resected disease; no RECIST translation in overt recurrence.
toxicity_burden: Low (injection-site reactions; no G3+ vaccine-attributed events)

counter_productive_moa.description: In an MSS immune-cold, bulky recurrent tumor, T-cell priming may not overcome the immunosuppressive stroma; setting mismatch is the core risk.

overall: The cleanest allele-matched mechanism and safety on the board, foreclosed by an MRD/adjuvant enrollment window that excludes this overt-recurrent patient.
